message_log.text: 🏋️ Evening Weight Training - Sept 6 Grade: 7/10 - solid, low-strain strength session that slotted in cleanly around your running load RECOVERY CONTEXT (athletedata, before the session) Readiness was strong going in: recovery score 80, readiness verdict "go_hard", HRV 53 (above your 60d baseline of 48), resting HR 47. TSB (start-of-day basis, using Sept 5's CTL 64.2 - ATL 79.4) sits at -15.2, so you were fatigued/absorbing load but not flashing red. VO2max 56, fitness age 20. COACH'S PLAN Scheduled as a strength session (60 min target), status completed - matches what you did (77.7 min). SUMMARY 77-minute strength session, avg HR just 83bpm (max 117bpm) - textbook low cardiovascular strain for a lifting day, exactly what you want between run sessions. Suffer score of 8 confirms this was easy on the aerobic system, all the work happening elsewhere. GOOD PARTS • Avg HR 83bpm for 77 minutes is very controlled - no cardiovascular stacking on top of your running fatigue • Session ran slightly over the 60-min target (77.7 min) without dragging your ACWR anywhere near a red zone • Body battery climbed steadily through the session (61 to 96 range across the evening block), showing you weren't digging into a big reserve deficit WATCH FOR • TSB at -15.2 (start-of-day) plus ramp_rate 0.8 means you're still net fatigued from the running block - keep this session's load easy/moderate rather than pushing new PRs on lifts right now • No zero-full-rest-day flag in the last 14 days - worth actually taking one soon given the fatigued form status OVERTRAINING CHECK: Moderate Reconciling the numbers: acwr sits at a sweet-spot 0.91, monotony 1.03 (healthy variability, not flatlined), and load_flag index is 0 with no active drivers - none of the anomaly signals are firing. But TSB at -15.2 (start-of-day) and the fatigued/absorbing-training form status, combined with zero full rest days in the past 14, mean you're running a real fatigue deficit even though this particular strength session barely dented it (avg HR 83bpm, dailyLoad only 25.9). Verdict: manageable now, but the lack of a genuine rest day is the actual lever - schedule one full rest day in the next 3-4 days before the next hard running session rather than letting TSB drift lower.

SAME-SEGMENT TREND The "sprint" benchmark segment improved meaningfully: 59s today vs 65s prior (July 13), and at a lower HR too - 172.4bpm vs 187.7bpmGOOD PARTS • All 14 surge reps landed in the 3:45-4:10/km window - pacing discipline was excellent even as HR drifted • Sprint benchmark: 59s @ 172bpm vs 65s @ 188bpm three months ago - faster and 15bpm cheaper • Best 400m at 91s shows real top-end speed is there when needed WATCH FOR • Surge HR ceiling breached this morning's 172bpm target from surge 4 onward, topping out at 188bpm (your all-time-ish max) by surge 12 - the surges became harder than "hit the paces, don't empty the tank" • Floats stopped truly recovering - HR sat 156-169bpm on the last several float segments instead of dropping toward 145-150bpm, meaning you were stacking fatigue rep to rep • Session ran 59min vs the 83min planned - you got the surge/float work in but cut the aerobic warmup/cooldown volume short OVERTRAINING CHECK: Moderate ACWR sits in the sweet spot at 0.94, monotony 1.03, and load_flag index is 0 with nothing flagged - no anomaly signals firing. But TSB is -8.5 (start-of-day) and you still haven't taken the full rest day flagged after yesterday's strength session and again in this morning's brief - 14 days now without one. Layer on today's HR pattern (surges creeping to 185-188bpm, floats not dropping below 150bpm) and this reads as a session run a notch harder than prescribed on a body that's still carrying fatigue. Nothing dangerous, but the rest-day debt is real: prioritize one full day off in the next 2-3 days before your next hard interval or hill session.
